name: Oracle Migration Assessment
description: Captures Oracle-specific dependencies, migration constraints, validation, licensing, lifecycle and target decisions that cannot be determined from automated discovery alone.

sections.title: Oracle Workload & Target
sections.description: Identify workload ownership, critical schemas, application dependencies and the intended target.

questions.text: Which schemas are in scope for this migration?
Are multiple applications or business units sharing this Oracle database?
Describe any application release, batch, reporting or interface schedules that constrain migration timing.
Who owns and can approve changes to PL/SQL code and database objects?
Which Oracle migration destination and target database version are being evaluated?
options: Oracle Database on Azure Virtual Machines
Azure SQL Managed Instance or SQL Database

questions.text: What data growth and capacity planning horizon must the Oracle target support?

sections.title: Oracle Features & Dependencies
sections.description: Confirm whether discovered Oracle capabilities are business-critical and how they may be replaced.

questions.text: Which discovered Oracle features are business-critical, removable or require replacement?
Are database links used in critical transaction or reporting paths?
Describe external systems reached through database links, gateways, queues or file access.
Can Oracle-specific PL/SQL packages and features be refactored if the target does not support them?
Does application behavior depend on Oracle-specific SQL or session semantics?
questions.helpText: Examples include empty strings treated as NULL, Oracle DATE behavior, NLS settings, sequence behavior, quoted identifiers, hints or implicit type conversions.

sections.title: Migration & Continuity
sections.description: Choose a supported migration workflow and confirm compatibility, connectivity and rollback prerequisites.

questions.text: Which migration workflow best fits the source, target and downtime requirements?
Which migration tools are approved or preferred?
Is Oracle GoldenGate already licensed and available for migration use?
Have source-to-target compatibility prerequisites been verified for the selected workflow?
questions.helpText: Check database version and patch level, platform endianness, character set, time zone file version, COMPATIBLE setting, encryption algorithm and target service restrictions.
options: Not applicable to the selected workflow

questions.text: Has secure network connectivity and sustained migration throughput to the target been tested with production-scale data?
Can source schema and application changes be frozen during the final migration and validation window?
Describe the required rollback method and rollback decision triggers if cutover validation fails.
Is a source and target coexistence period required after cutover?

sections.title: Validation & Cutover Readiness
sections.description: Define the evidence, rehearsals and approvals required before production cutover.

questions.text: Which source-to-target validation checks are required for acceptance?
options: Date, time zone and character encoding checks

questions.text: Who owns data reconciliation and has authority to accept documented variances?
Have representative peak-load performance baselines and target acceptance thresholds been agreed?
options: Baselines captured but thresholds not agreed

questions.text: What is the status of the production-scale migration rehearsal?
Who provides final business, application, database, security and operations sign-off for cutover?

sections.title: Licensing, Security & Operations
sections.description: Capture Oracle licensing, access and post-migration operating requirements.

questions.text: Which separately licensed Oracle options or management packs are currently used?
Are there Oracle Wallet, TDE, HSM or external key-management dependencies?
Describe required authentication integrations such as LDAP, Kerberos, proxy users or enterprise users.
Which Oracle security and audit controls must be preserved or replaced on the target?
Who will own backup, patching, monitoring and performance tuning on the target platform?
What criteria and approvals are required to decommission the source and terminate Oracle licenses or support?
